A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEMoN research work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix G report original detection, downstream training, ablation, pretraining, and manual label-verification results.

after.justification: Sections 5–6 and the appendices retain original empirical results and add experiments on web corpora, additional classification datasets, validation requirements, and corruption robustness.

M1.justification: The three-term score, neighbor weighting, LEMoNOPT/LEMoNFIX variants, and hyperparameter-search procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure; the corrected weighting subscript in Equation (3) matches the parameter already described in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds miniImageNet and StanfordCars with real annotation noise, CC3M and DataComp filtering/pretraining experiments, VTAB transfer evaluation, and CIFAR-10C corruption testing. These substantially expand coverage beyond v1's six datasets to web-scale training and shifted evaluation conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds Discrepancy to classification and captioning comparisons, adapted VDC to captioning, and additional Thomas–Kovashka scores and combinations in Table I.13. Captioning Datamap's documented score changes from a ratio to a product of loss statistics. Downstream Figure 3 adds Discrepancy and removes AUM and Datamap from that comparison.

E3.justification: Reported downstream captioning settings change from five to ten maximum epochs, learning rate 1e-5 to 1e-4, and top-k sampling to four-beam search (v1 Appendix F.2; v2 H.2). Classification changes from at most 15 epochs and averaging across learning rates to at most 30 epochs with learning-rate selection and early stopping. Added experiments introduce transfer, validation-subsampling, and corruption-evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds score-component combinations, validation-set-size sensitivity, empirical checks of theoretical assumptions, checkpoint-selection controls, runtime comparisons, and corruption robustness. Conversely, v1 Figures G.3–G.4, examining detection metrics versus downstream accuracy and caption-filtering thresholds, are removed. The scope of supplementary analysis changes substantially.

E5.justification: The three-run mean/standard-deviation reporting and manual study's binomial confidence intervals remain. Appendix A.2 newly applies Shapiro–Wilk normality tests, including subsampling classification distances and testing caption-distance distributions. There is no reported increase in the main experiments' repeat count.

E6.justification: Many existing numerical entries change: for example, Table 2 reports CIFAR-10 LEMoNOPT F1 as 93.1 in v1 and 92.0 in v2. Extensive new results include CC3M average zero-shot accuracy of 10.83% for LEMoNFIX, 10.34% for CLIP filtering, and 14.08% without filtering (Table I.15). Revised downstream captioning scores use changed training and decoding settings, so they do not establish same-setting gains across versions.

T1.justification: v2 introduces paraphrase-set and Gaussian-distance assumptions, a neighborhood-score AUROC theorem, and a better-than-random-signal lemma with proofs. v1's CLIP-loss robustness proposition is removed, while its noisy-label separation proposition is substantially reformulated as a Lipschitz perturbation bound in Appendix A.3. These are substantive mathematical revisions, not relocation alone.

C1.justification: The central claims of multimodal-neighbor error detection and improved downstream training remain. The introduction replaces earlier F1-based superiority claims with more qualified AUROC advantages on three of four classification and three of four captioning datasets. The abstract also explicitly foregrounds theoretical justification and quantifies downstream captioning improvements.

C2.justification: v2 hypothesizes that noisy CC3M captions retain useful word associations, explaining why filtering can underperform using the full corpus. Its new impact statement discusses disproportionate removal of rare or minority examples and recommends expert review. It also expands component-importance and captioning-headroom interpretations, while removing v1's explicit limitation concerning untested instance-dependent noise.

D1.justification: v2 adds selected hyperparameters for individual datasets and methods, baseline reference-set and checkpoint details, VDC model/prompt adaptations, and web-corpus preprocessing and training instructions. These materially extend v1's search-space and hardware disclosures. Reproducibility remains limited by conflicting split descriptions for the added classification datasets in Table 1, Section 5.1, and Appendix D.1.

R1.justification: A new multimodal-neighborhood subsection and Appendix B position LEMoN against Thomas and Kovashka (2022), distinguishing semantic diversity from label-error detection and relating their scores to LEMoN's components. Additional neighborhood, data-cleaning, and benchmark literature substantially expands the research positioning beyond citation updates.

P1.justification: The seven-section main structure and much of the existing method and experimental prose remain. Editing refines wording and definitions, converts the contribution summary into bullets, adds a plain-language algorithm explanation and notation glossary, and adjusts appendix organization. Most expansion accompanies the substantive additions assessed separately.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Tables 2–3 are reorganized across datasets, with fuller results including AUPRC placed in the appendix; Figure 3 is redrawn with different comparators. New histograms, sensitivity and robustness plots, algorithm/notation displays, and experimental tables substantially change presentation, alongside removal of Figures G.3–G.4.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence about real web-scale use and labeled-validation requirements through CC3M/DataComp experiments, validation-size tests, closer competing methods, and robustness analyses. Reporting that filtering can underperform the full corpus makes the applicability claims more informative, while selected configurations improve reproducibility. Removed analyses and inconsistent split/table reporting remain drawbacks, but the expanded evidence materially strengthens assessment of the method's effectiveness and limits.
